EasyCalculator

🇮🇳 Simple, transparent financial calculators for India — built in R

A growing toolbox of financial calculators — income tax today, with GST and loan calculators on the way — each usable for one person or a whole portfolio in a single line of R.

📦 Install · 🚀 Quick start · 🧰 Calculators · 🧮 Tax calculator · 🗺️ Roadmap · 🤝 Contributing

[!WARNING] ### 🚧 Under review — major improvements on the way EasyCalculator is currently under active review, and significant improvements are being worked on. 🛠️ In the meantime you may run into bugs, rough edges or results that don’t match the official rules. Please pardon any problems you find at this stage 🙏 — and if you spot one, opening an issue would be a big help. Thank you for your patience and support! 💙

✨ Why EasyCalculator?

Feature What you get
🧰 Many calculators, one package Income tax today; GST and loan calculators planned — all sharing one consistent style.
⚡ One-liner tax_payable(1150000) — done.
👥 Bulk-ready Pass a data frame of hundreds of people and get one tidy result back.
📊 Data-driven rules Rates, slabs and limits live in plain data tables, not buried in code — easy to audit and update.
🔍 Transparent output A step-by-step breakdown, not just a final number.

🧰 Calculators

Calculator Function Status
🧮 Income tax (old vs new regime) tax_payable() ✅ Available
🧾 GST gst_calculator() 🗓️ Planned
🏦 Loan scheduler loan_schedular() 🗓️ Planned

Every calculator is documented on the reference page of the package website.

📦 Installation 

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("Poduval/EasyCalculator")
library(EasyCalculator)

💡 Requires R ≥ 4.1.0 and the plyr package.

🚀 Quick start

The examples below use the income tax calculator, the first one available.

👤 A single taxpayer 

# New regime (default), financial year 2024
tax_payable(1150000)

# Old regime
tax_payable(1150000, tax_regime = "old")

👥 Many taxpayers at once 

people <- data.frame(
  id            = c(1, 2, 3),
  annual_income = c(1400000, 2000000, 3000000)
)

tax_payable(people)

💼 With investment deductions (old regime) 

person <- data.frame(
  id            = 1,
  annual_income = 1500000,
  tax_regime    = "old",
  declared_NPS  = 50000,
  declared_80C  = 150000,
  declared_80D  = 25000
)

tax_payable(person)

🧮 Tax calculator

tax_payable() computes Indian income tax under the Old and New regimes. It handles the standard deduction, investment deductions (NPS, 80C, 80D, 24B, 80TTA — capped at statutory limits, old regime), Section 87A rebate and 4% surcharge/cess.

🔧 Inputs

Column Required Description
id ✅ Identifier for each taxpayer
annual_income ✅ Gross annual income (₹)
financial_year ➖ Defaults to 2024
tax_regime ➖ "new" (default) or "old"
declared_NPS declared_80C declared_80D declared_24B declared_80TTA ➖ Declared investments / deductions (old regime only)

📤 Output

A data frame of class ITR with a readable print() method and full detail underneath:

Column Meaning
💰 annual_income Income you supplied
🧾 taxable_amount Income after exemptions and deductions
📉 rebate_under_investments Deductions allowed after applying limits
🧮 tax_from_income_slab Tax computed from the slabs
🎁 rebate_under_87A Section 87A rebate applied
🏛️ tax_surcharge 4% surcharge / cess
✅ tax_value The tax you owe

📈 FY 2024 slabs

🆕 New regime 🕰️ Old regime
Income (₹) Rate
0 – 3,00,000 0%
3,00,000 – 6,00,000 5%
6,00,000 – 9,00,000 10%
9,00,000 – 12,00,000 15%
12,00,000 – 15,00,000 20%
Above 15,00,000 30%
Income (₹) Rate
0 – 2,50,000 0%
2,50,000 – 5,00,000 5%
5,00,000 – 10,00,000 20%
Above 10,00,000 30%

🏷️ Deduction limits (old regime, FY 2024)

Section Covers Limit (₹)
🏦 NPS National Pension Scheme 50,000
🛡️ 80C Tax-saving investments 1,50,000
⚕️ 80D Medical insurance 1,50,000
🏠 24B Home-loan interest 2,00,000
💳 80TTA Savings-account interest 10,000

⚙️ How it works 

flowchart LR
    A["👤 Income &<br/>declarations"] --> B["🧾 Basic exemption<br/>+ standard deduction"]
    B --> C["💼 Investment deductions<br/>(capped, old regime)"]
    C --> D["📊 Slab tax"]
    D --> E["🎁 Section 87A<br/>rebate"]
    E --> F["🏛️ 4% surcharge<br/>/ cess"]
    F --> G["✅ Tax payable"]

    classDef input fill:#E3F2FD,stroke:#1E88E5,color:#0D47A1;
    classDef step fill:#FFF8E1,stroke:#FB8C00,color:#E65100;
    classDef out fill:#E8F5E9,stroke:#43A047,color:#1B5E20;
    class A input;
    class B,C,D,E,F step;
    class G out;

The tax calculator is deliberately small and layered (new calculators follow the same generic → method → data-table pattern):

flowchart TB
    G["tax_payable(x, ...)<br/><i>S3 generic</i>"] --> N["tax_payable.default<br/><i>numeric vector</i>"]
    G --> DF["tax_payable.data.frame<br/><i>the engine</i>"]
    N -->|builds a data frame| DF
    DF --> T[("📚 data.* tables<br/>slabs · rebates · limits")]
    DF --> P["print.ITR<br/><i>friendly summary</i>"]

🧠 Rules are data, not code. Every slab, exemption and limit is stored in a table keyed by tax_regime and financial_year, so supporting a new Budget is mostly a matter of adding rows.

⚠️ Good to know

  • 📅 For the tax calculator, only FY 2024 rules are included today. Unknown years fall back to 2024 in data-frame input.
  • 🚧 The package is under review; expect changes and improvements, and please report any issues you find.
  • 🧑‍⚖️ This package is an aid for estimation and learning — not professional tax advice. Always verify against the official Income Tax Department rules or consult a qualified tax professional.
